rounds.text: Almondz Global Securities Ltd trades at an attractive valuation, with a price-to-earnings ratio of 10.4x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 1.21x against a book value of 15.5 [E2], while offering a compelling discount compared to sector benchmarks like a P/E of 11.08x versus 19.59x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 8.8x versus 13.53x [E11]. The underlying fundamental growth is exceptional, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 33% [E17] and a staggering compounded profit growth of 88% [E21], alongside a recent quarterly operating margin expansion of 4 percentage points to 22% in June 2026 [E31]. Furthermore, the business is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E37], comfortable short-term liquidity indicated by a current ratio of 3.17x [E38], and shrinking borrowings down to 49 crore in March 2026 [E39]. Technical momentum fully supports this undervaluation thesis, as the stock sits above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E50, E51], while a quantitative DCF model estimates a substantial margin of safety of 54.4% [E46]. Conceded: the company displays negative operating cash flow of 4 crore and negative free cash flow of 6 crore for March 2026 alongside a zero dividend yield [E4, E35, E36].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 10.4x [E1], a P/B of 1.21x [E2], and an EV/EBITDA of 8.8x [E11]. However, that low multiple is entirely justified by severe quality and cash generation deficits, notably negative operating cash flow of Rs -4 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -6 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], alongside a cash conversion ratio of -0.14x [E34]. Furthermore, reported earnings are artificially inflated by Rs. 18.4 Cr of other income [E65], and the business pays a zero dividend yield despite claiming profitability [E4, E62]. The bull points to exceptional trailing sales and profit growth [E17, E21], but ignores that historical return on equity is mediocre—with a 10-year median ROE of just 8% and a 3-year median of 9% [E26, E28, E64]—while institutional participation is actively fleeing through negative money flows and falling foreign ownership down to 0.08% [E42, E44]. Finally, the cited technical momentum and moving averages [E50, E51] provide scant comfort given the company's historical volatility of 63.6% and a catastrophic peak-to-trough drawdown of -92.6% [E53, E54].
